title.en: Six Miles of Walking, One Mile of Progress

dek.zh: 船被浮冰压毁后，沙克尔顿带队在冰上分批搬运、艰难行进，苦干四天之后决定在一块厚浮冰上扎营等待。他自己写下了理由：雪面太软走不远，而附近可能开出水道。
dek.en: After the pack ice crushed their ship, Shackleton's party struggled across the floes, ferrying loads in relays; after four days of hard effort he decided to camp on a thick floe and wait. He wrote down his reasons: the snow was too soft to get far, and leads might open close by.

paras.zh: 南极的浮冰上，沙克尔顿的船被冰压得扶正无望，只能放弃。人还活着，食品和装备也还在。他写下新的任务，只有一句：「The task is to reach land with all the members of the Expedition」——任务是让全体队员抵达陆地。
paras.en: On the Antarctic pack ice, Shackleton's ship was crushed by the ice beyond all hope of ever being righted, and the men had to abandon her. They were alive and well, and their stores and equipment were still in hand. He set down the new task in a single sentence: "The task is to reach land with all the members of the Expedition."

paras.zh: 可怎么到陆地？冰面是松软的湿雪，装备要分批来回搬运，一天下来直线只前进约一英里。苦干四天之后的第二天早上，他决定停下来扎营。
paras.en: But how to reach land? The surface was loose, wet snow, and loads had to be ferried back and forth in relays; a day's march gained about a mile in a straight line. On the morning after four days of hard effort, he decided to stop and camp.

heading.en: The Original Plan, and the Two-Pound Rule

paras.zh: 原计划要宏大得多：横穿队伍立刻出发，踏上1800英里的行程，希望在五个月内穿越极点，抵达罗斯海一侧的基地。船被压毁之后，任务换成了另一件事——让全队上岸。
paras.en: The plan he began with was far grander: "the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once," he wrote, "in the hope of accomplishing the march across the Pole and reaching the Ross Sea base in five months." Eighteen hundred miles, the Pole, a base on the far side of the continent. Once the ice had crushed Endurance, the task became something else entirely: get the whole party onto land.

paras.zh: 在被他们称为抛弃营的地方，装备经历了一次大幅筛选。他决定给每人发一整套全新的 Burberry 外衣和内衣，再加新袜子；同时定下规矩：个人物品不得超过两磅，除了最必需的东西，一律不上路。用他的原话，负担不起多余的重量。
paras.en: At a place they named Dump Camp, the equipment went through a severe weeding-out. He decided to issue each man a complete new set of Burberrys — Burberry coats — and underclothing, along with a supply of new socks. At the same time he fixed the rule: "personal gear must not exceed two pounds per man," which meant nothing but bare necessaries would go on the march. In his words, they could not afford to cumber themselves with unnecessary weight.

paras.zh: 这次筛选也落在一些小东西上，后文再细说。
paras.en: The weeding-out reached small personal things too; more on that below.

heading.en: Four Days of Marching, Then Camp

paras.zh: 弃船时他写道：船已被压碎，再没有扶正的希望；大家活着、健康，手头有食品和装备去面对眼前的活儿。写完任务那句之后，他又添了一句：「It is hard to write what I feel.」很难写下自己的感受。
paras.en: When they abandoned the ship he wrote: the ship was crushed beyond all hope of ever being righted; they were alive and well, and had stores and equipment to meet the work in front of them. After the sentence about the task he added one more line: "It is hard to write what I feel."

paras.zh: 接着是清点。用他的话说，不能为多余的装备付出代价，器材被彻底筛了一遍。他给每人换发一整套新外衣和内衣，外加新袜子。
paras.en: Then came the counting and culling. In his words, they could not afford to carry unnecessary gear, and the equipment was sorted through with a heavy hand. He issued every man a full new set of outer clothing and underclothing, plus new socks.

paras.zh: 规矩定得很硬：每人个人物品不得超过两磅。除最必需的东西外什么都不带，这句话被他写成了死命令，而不是建议。
paras.en: The rule that followed was hard-edged: personal gear must not exceed two pounds per man. Nothing beyond bare necessaries was to be taken. He wrote it as an order, not a suggestion.

paras.zh: 于是有了那个读完忘不掉的细节：金币被扔掉，照片被留下；他还从王后赠给船的那本圣经上撕下扉页，那一页上有她亲笔写的字。
paras.en: And so the detail that stays with you: "sovereigns were thrown away and photographs were kept." He tore the fly-leaf out of the Bible the Queen had given to the ship, the page with her own writing on it.

paras.zh: 行军的账很难看。一天下来，直线只前进了约一英里；为了绕开障碍，实际走过的距离至少两英里；而分批搬运、来回接力，把当天走过的路程推到了六英里。也就是说，脚步花了六份，位置只挪了一份。
paras.en: The arithmetic of the march made ugly reading. Over one day's going they gained about one mile in a direct line. The detours forced on them meant the ground actually travelled was at least two miles. And the relays — loads ferried back and forth — pushed the day's marching up to six miles. Six parts of footwork bought one part of position.

paras.zh: 苦干四天之后的第二天，天冷而平静，还是那种湿雪。他看清了两件事：以眼下松软的雪面，加上四天苦干换来的那点成果，走不了多远；同时，附近有可能开出水道，那样就能划船向西北方向去找陆地。两件事合起来指向同一个决定——找一块更结实的浮冰扎营，等条件更有利时再做第二次挣脱冰牢的尝试。
paras.en: The next day, after four days of hard effort, broke cold and still, with the same wet snow. In the clearing light he could see the situation plainly. With the surface as loose as it was, and given how little they had to show for four days of strenuous effort, they would never get any great distance. And there was a second possibility to weigh: leads might open close to them, which would let them row north-west to where they might find land. The two considerations pointed one way. He decided to find a more solid floe, camp there, and stay until conditions were more favourable for a second attempt to escape from their icy prison.

paras.zh: 他们把帐篷和全部家当搬到一块又厚又重的老浮冰上，距沉船约一英里半，在那里扎下营，取名海洋营。
paras.en: Tents and everything else were moved to a thick, heavy old floe about one and a half miles from the wreck, and there they made their camp. They called it Ocean Camp.

paras.zh: 后来他们又换了营地，叫耐心营，在那里住了将近三个半月。
paras.en: Later they moved camp again, to a place they called Patience Camp, and lived there for nearly three and a half months.

heading.zh: 把停止写成有下一步的动作
heading.en: Making a Stop That Carries a Next Step

paras.zh: 一种解释是，这个决定的关键不在停，而在停的方式。他没有写成我们不走了，而是写成等条件更有利时做第二次尝试：营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望——水道可能在附近开出来，那时可以下水划船。等待因此有对象、有触发条件，不是躺平。作者推断，正是这个写法让队伍能把力气省下来，而不必每天用六份脚步换一份位置。
paras.en: Read the decision one way and what matters is not that he stopped, but how he wrote the stop. He did not frame it as a declaration that they were finished with moving. He framed it as a second attempt to be made once conditions grew more favourable: the camp went onto a more solid floe, and the reasoning carried a specific hope — leads opening nearby, boats in the water, land somewhere to the north-west. Waiting therefore had an object and a trigger; it was not simply lying down. The author's inference is that this way of writing the decision is what let the party bank its strength, instead of buying one mile of position with six miles of walking, day after day.

paras.zh: 另一种解释是关于取舍的标准（作者推断）：金币在冰上派不上用场，照片和一页有亲笔字的扉页也换不来什么，但后两者被留下了。他在这几段里没有说明原因；也许那道上限筛的只是重量，也许只是个人偏好，两种说法都超出了他写下的内容。
paras.en: A second reading, and it is the author's, concerns the standard behind the choices. Gold coins were of no use on the ice; the photographs and a page with the Queen's handwriting could not buy anything either, yet those were the things kept. He gives no reason in these passages. Perhaps the limit screened only for weight; perhaps it was personal preference. Both go beyond what he wrote.

paras.zh: 作者提出的替代选择（他没有写自己考虑过这些）：比如把队伍分成两支，一支维持最低限度的探路，一支守营保存体力；或者先派少数人轻装去试水道。这类做法都要把队伍拆开。列在这里只是想说明，那天的决定不是唯一的可能，却和当时手里的条件对得上。
paras.en: Then there are alternatives the author raises for the sake of argument; nothing suggests Shackleton weighed them himself. The party could have been split in two, one half keeping up a minimal reconnaissance while the other held the camp and conserved its strength. Or a few men might have gone ahead lightly loaded, to feel out the leads. Both would have meant splitting the party. They are listed here only to show that the decision of that day was not the only possibility, though it did match the conditions in front of them.

paras.zh: 场景一：一个创业团队的融资没谈成，原计划已经不成立。负责人第一次全员会上最有用的，也许就是像那句“任务是让全体队员抵达陆地”一样，用一句话说清新的目标：现在要做到什么，怎么算做到。
paras.en: Scenario one: a start-up's fundraising has fallen through and the original plan no longer stands. At the first all-hands meeting, the most useful thing the founder can do may be what that line did, "The task is to reach land with all the members of the Expedition": state the new goal in one sentence, what has to be achieved now and how you will know.

paras.zh: 场景二：个人创作。连续投稿，退稿的间隙越来越长，你开始怀疑该不该每天硬写凑数。此时可以先做那次两磅的筛选：留下真正必需的（读、记、改），扔掉看起来体面但拖慢你的部分；然后给等待定一个复查日，比如两个月后看一次信号再决定。停下来不等于停笔，只是不再用六份力气换一份进度。
paras.en: Scenario two: creative work of your own. You have been submitting steadily, the gaps between rejections keep stretching, and you have begun to wonder whether forcing out words every day is worth it. This is the moment for the two-pound sort. Keep what is genuinely necessary — reading, notes, revision. Drop what looks respectable but only slows you down. Then give the waiting a review date: in two months, you check the signals and decide again. Stopping does not mean putting down the pen. It means no longer trading six measures of effort for one measure of progress.

paras.zh: 本篇的全部过程都出自沙克尔顿本人的叙述（这里用的是1920年印本的 OCR 文本），是当事人、领导者的记述，其中有些段落像是当时的日记。没有取得其他队员的日记作对照，营地里别人怎么想、是否同意这个决定，证据里没有，本篇也不替他们猜测心理。
paras.en: Everything in this piece comes from Shackleton's own narrative, read here through the OCR text of the 1920 printing: the account of a participant who led the party, parts of which read like a contemporary diary. No other member's diary has been brought in for comparison. What the rest of the camp thought, and whether anyone questioned the decision, is not in the evidence, and this piece does not put feelings in their mouths.

paras.zh: 文本是 OCR，有讹字，引用只取清晰片段，个别有讹字的词不加引号照抄。所有数字——1800英里、两磅、一英里、六英里、一英里半、三个半月——都出自他的记述，未与别的记录核对。本篇也不写此后获救的过程，那部分不在这份证据包的覆盖范围内。
paras.en: The text is machine-read, and it carries errors. Quotations are taken only from clean stretches; a few damaged words are reproduced without quotation marks. All the figures — 1,800 miles, two pounds, one mile, six miles, one and a half miles, three and a half months — come from his account and have not been checked against any other record. Nor does this piece tell the story of the rescue that followed; that falls outside the evidence gathered here.

scenario.zh: 你带一个小团队做有交付期的项目，投入连续几周增加，关键指标却只挪很小一段；与此同时，一个外部条件（合作方窗口、季节、审批）可能在一两个月内变好。继续加人硬推，还是收拢资源，等窗口成熟再做第二次冲刺？
scenario.en: You lead a small team on a project with a delivery deadline. Weeks of rising input have moved the key metric by only a little. At the same time, an external condition — a partner's window, a season, an approval — may improve within a month or two. Do you keep adding people and pushing, or gather your resources and wait for the window, then make a second, concentrated push?

question.zh: 什么信号出现时，你会把继续推进改成停下来等？你给自己定的复查日是哪一天？
question.en: What signal would tell you to turn continued effort into a deliberate wait? And what review date do you set for yourself?

assumptions.zh: 每周追加投入，但关键指标每周只前进很小一段；外部条件在未来一到两个月内有可能变好；团队的体力和预算是有限的，且分散使用会让两边都做不成。
assumptions.en: Extra effort goes in every week, but the key metric advances only a little each week. The external condition may improve within one to two months. The team's energy and budget are finite, and splitting them would leave both halves unable to finish.

steps.zh:
先做一次两磅式的筛选：把资源分成必需与可弃，给每个人的负担设上限
把真实产出分开记：直线进展算一份，绕路和来回搬运的消耗单算
若直线进展持续远低于消耗，收拢队伍到一个稳固的据点，并定下明确的复查日
条件好转时做一次集中的第二次尝试，而不是每天小步硬推
steps.en:
Run a two-pound sort first: divide resources into indispensable and disposable, and cap each person's load
Record real output separately: direct progress counts as one figure, detours and ferrying are counted as their own cost
If direct progress keeps running far below the cost, gather the team onto a firm base and set an explicit review date
When conditions improve, make one concentrated second attempt instead of grinding out small steps daily

alternative.zh: 作者提出的另一种做法：不整体停下，而是分两支，一支维持最低限度的试推，一支专门盯外部窗口。代价是人力分散，两支都可能不够用。
alternative.en: Another course the author raises: instead of stopping wholesale, split in two — one part keeps up a minimal probe while the other watches the external window. The cost is a divided workforce, and neither half may prove large enough.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全部来自沙克尔顿本人的叙述（本篇用1920年印本的 OCR 文本），是当事人、领导者的记述，没有其他队员的日记作对照；OCR 有讹字，引用只取清晰片段；文中数字均出自该记述，未经独立核对；本篇不涉及此后的获救过程。
uncertainty_note.en: Everything here comes from Shackleton's own narrative (this piece uses the OCR text of the 1920 printing): the account of the participant who led the party, with no other member's diary for comparison. The OCR carries errors, and quotations are drawn only from clean stretches. Every figure in the piece comes from that account and has not been independently verified. The rescue that followed is not covered here.

preheader.zh: 两磅个人物品、一页圣经扉页，和一个停下来的决定。
preheader.en: Two pounds of personal gear, a torn flyleaf, and a decision to stop.

sources.citation: Ernest Shackleton, South: The Story of Shackleton's Last Expedition, 1914–1917 (1920 printing; archive.org OCR)

what.zh: 沙克尔顿本人的叙述，第四、五章写弃船与海洋营。
what.en: Shackleton's own account; chapters 4–5 cover the loss of the ship and Ocean Camp.

episode.action: abandon the march across the ice and camp on a floe
